A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 23-page versions of the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A and B can be reliably matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning evaluations with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, including benchmark accuracies, fixed-configuration ablations, and compute analyses in Table 1 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark accuracies in Table 1, ablations in Tables 2 and 7, and supplementary compute analyses in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix B retain the same planning, tool selection, compute selection, search procedures, PRM scoring, and final trajectory selection. No method component, model, or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same mathematical-reasoning coverage: MATH-500, AIME24, and AMO-Bench. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Direct, Direct + PRM Selection, and Dynamic comparisons. Tables 2 and 7 retain the same fixed CoT/Self-Reflection configurations using Best-of-N, Beam Search, and Lookahead.

E3.justification: Section 3 retains the same models, K=10 multi-iteration setting, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.9, 1024-token generation limit, and Satori evaluation protocol. Evaluation metrics and the fixed-configuration parameter and iteration grids also match.

E4.justification: The fixed-configuration ablations, difficulty-level analysis, tool/strategy usage analysis, and accuracy-compute comparisons are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same supplementary analyses and direct-versus-adaptive worked example.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same inference-iteration reporting and point accuracies. Neither adds evaluation-seed information, run-to-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative outcomes match throughout the main text and appendices, including Tables 1, 2, and 5-7 and Figures 2-5. For example, Table 1 retains Dynamic + PRM Selection accuracy of 65.4% and 81.4% on MATH-500 for Llama and Qwen, respectively.

T1.justification: The trajectory-reward and selection equations, FLOP and compute-intensity definitions, and Appendix A.1 notation are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about verifier-guided adaptive reasoning, accuracy gains over static inference, and compute utilization. Their scientific meaning and scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of difficulty-dependent gains and accuracy-conditional efficiency. Section 5 preserves the limitations concerning PRM reliability, heuristic control, latency overhead, and untested generalization beyond mathematics.

D1.justification: The decoding settings, single RTX 5090 with 32 GB memory, evaluation-code attribution, and role-specific prompt templates in Appendix B are unchanged. No implementation or code/data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning relative to fixed inference strategies, adaptive compute allocation, and process reward models.

P1.justification: Front-matter edits expand Ahmed Mohsin to Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, add equal-contribution markers, and revise affiliations and dates, including Ayesha Mohsin's affiliation. Scientific prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 2 to page 3, shifting Figure 2 downward and reflowing surrounding text. Figure and table content, designs, and captions are retained; the appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies author attribution and relocates Figure 1, while preserving the scientific exposition, evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information. The identical appendices and unchanged results establish that these limited editorial and layout changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
